content:
Subscribing to the mailing list does not appear to work for me, I'm not getting any response back. I sent two mails to rust-for-linux+subscribe@vger.kernel.org, one without any mention, one with subscribe in the subject and a short body message. Checking the mail server log reveals: "delivery 107166: success: 44.238.234.78 accepted message. Remote host said: 250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as 0B626606A31C" and before that "as 5AD24606A31C", but no connection attempt back.

So either vger.kernel.org treats my mail as spam or something is broken. (I have just verified via http://multirbl.valli.org (via option of sending an actual email) that my outgoing mail server is not on blacklists (uribl.com shows but seems broken, their own checker has me not listed); I also haven't had delivery problems for a while.)
Did you make sure to send a plain text message without html?
Subscribing to the lists may not be the best way to consume them. There is tooling such as korgalore and lei that may work better for you.

Andreas Hindborg said:

Did you make sure to send a plain text message without html?

Yes. Here's the exact second message as passed to sendmail -t:

Return-Path: <ch@christianjaeger.ch>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain;
 charset=utf-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit
Subject: subscribe
From: Christian Jaeger <ch@christianjaeger.ch>
To: rust-for-linux+subscribe@vger.kernel.org
Message-ID: <nyy768pnr7hintpnxj3-1794562354@christianjaeger.ch>

Hi

Please subscribe me to the rust-for-linux mailing list.

Christian.

Andreas Hindborg said:

Subscribing to the lists may not be the best way to consume them. There is tooling such as korgalore and lei that may work better for you.

Good to know. But I'm currently primarily planning to follow discussions and I like reading threads in a mail client better than in the online archive, and that's not something those tools seem to help with.
(I noticed claimed NNTP support and might try this.)
lei allows you to define a filter and subscribe to that filter. It will output the emails in a maildir. You can then use your favorite tooling to consume that maildir.
I'm quite certain the filter can be for instance an email address.
I think korgalore is similar, but instead of local maildir output, it can dump the output at your email provider via imap.
I sent a message to the help desk about it.
Thanks to both of you. I'll check lei (but it might also be nicest if it just works "normally" :), I'll see what comes out of it.
